text: The bard was a rank in Celtic society. His words held the power to bless and to curse. In Gaul he was the lowest order of poets. He sang the songs and recited the old tales. He acted as a historian as well. He could not change the facts of a story or a family line. The higher orders were the diviners and the druids. In Ireland a young bard learned his craft. He memorized hundreds of narratives. Then he learnt to compose fast in a fixed form, and the craft was bound to prophecy and the working of spells. The greatest poet was the satirist. His sharp words could bring low an unworthy king. The line between the poet, the judge, and the prophet was never sharp.
